results.title: Democratic Congress could complicate S. Korea's nuclear sub plans, Trump-Kim summit: experts
results.content: WASHINGTON — Democratic control of the U.S. Congress could make it harder for South Korea to acquire nuclear-powered submarines and limit President Donald Trump's ability to reach a deal with North Korea, even as he may seek another summit with leader Kim Jong-un, according to experts Wednesday. The assessments came after the Democratic Party scored a landslide victory in Tuesday's midterm elections, with the party poised to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, dealing a major political blow to Trump. Andrew Yeo, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, said Democrats could be more reluctant than Republicans to support South Korea's efforts to acquire nuclear-powered submarines because of concerns about the spread of nuclear technology. results.title: Korean celebrities reveal painful school bullying experiences
results.content: Korean television personality Lee Hye-sung has opened up about her painful experience of being bullied during her school years, drawing renewed attention to similar revelations by celebrities including actor Park Seo-joon, singer Sung Si-kyung and travel YouTuber KwakTube. On Friday, Lee discussed the bestselling self-help book "The Courage to Be Disliked" on her YouTube channel, Lee Hye-sung's 1% Book Club, offering advice to people struggling with school bullying and social exclusion. "If you think school is the only community where you belong, it can be incredibly painful when you're bullied or can't make friends," Lee said. "I've been through it myself." Reflecting on her middle school years, Lee said she had struggled to see beyond the difficult circumstances she faced at the time. "When I was younger, in middle school, I couldn't think that way.
